mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4.5% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative when the trigger occurs, or the effect is statistically insignificant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-force participation reduces risk aversion among investors.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5% in the current month
failure_condition: In regimes where employment is expanding, the signal does not produce statistically significant positive returns (p > 0.10), or the effect reverses direction in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (household utilization) rises above 17% for two consecutive months, it indicates accelerating demand, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite the trigger, or the pattern persists for >3 months without a positive return in any 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO above 110 (2017=100 index) suggests supply-side constraints, which, when combined with a rising CPIAUCSL, produces a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investor uncertainty rises.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 110 AND CPIAUCSL rising over the previous 2 months
failure_condition: In periods of excess supply (INDPRO < 110), the interaction does not produce a significant negative return, or the effect is reversed (positive returns) when demand proxies are also falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as lower policy rates lower discounting of expected profits.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the policy rate does not decline as expected, or 5-day forward returns remain negative despite the policy path.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) above 135,000 in a month when UNRATE is below 4%, signals a tight labor market and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 135,000 AND UNRATE < 4% in the current month
failure_condition: The effect is absent when unemployment is rising (UNRATE > 5%), or the return is negative despite the labor signal in expanding economies.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (real GDP chained) of at least 2% followed by a rebound month produces a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates a bottom in economic activity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls >2% for two consecutive months then rebounds in the third month
failure_condition: No significant return in the 60-day window after the pattern, or the pattern is not followed by a rebound month.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls for three consecutive months below its 12-month moving average while HOUST is flat, it indicates weak demand and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for three consecutive months AND HOUST flat
failure_condition: The pattern recurs during periods of excess demand (HOUST rising), or the return is positive when the supply signal occurs.
